<thought>Analyzing the 13C NMR data, methyl carbons (CH₃) usually appear upfield around 10–30 ppm. The observed carbon signals are at 138.76, 131.45 (×2), 130.59 (×2), 121.30, 43.47, and 38.60 ppm. None fall within the typical methyl region, and the higher‑field signals (38–44 ppm) correspond to other carbon types (e.g., methylene or carbon attached to heteroatoms). Therefore, the molecule contains no CH₃ groups.</thought>
